captions.detailed: A mountain bike front suspension fork assembly featuring a wide black crown and two telescoping lower stanchion legs. The upper inner tubes are finished in silver, sliding into matte black lower legs via a prismatic joint. At the top, a tapered threadless steerer tube is clamped by a two-bolt stem, which holds a set of wide, slightly swept-back grey handlebars with black grips. The entire steering assembly can rotate relative to the frame mount on a revolute joint.
captions.instruction: Create an articulated 3D model of a mountain bike air-suspension fork with handlebars. The model should include telescoping lower stanchion legs with prismatic sliding joints, a crown, a steering tube, and a stem clamping a wide set of handlebars, with a revolute joint for steering rotation.
captions.factory: Construct the assembly using an ArticulatedObject. Create the main frame/head tube as a fixed reference cylinder. Model the steering column (steerer, stem, handlebars, and upper fork crown) using cylindrical sweeps for the swept handlebars, cylinders for the steerer and stem, and boxes for the crown, connecting this assembly via a revolute joint to the head tube. Create the lower fork sliders (stanchions and dropouts) using cylinders and boxes, and connect them to the upper inner tubes using a prismatic joint to simulate suspension travel.
